condition: Hypertension (High Blood Pressure): Awareness, Symptoms, and When to Seek Care

source.title: Module for ASHA on Non-Communicable Diseases: Chapter 3: Hypertension
source.publisher: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Government of India / National Health Mission

scope_note: AIRA covers hypertension awareness, warning signs, lifestyle measures, and triage only. Diagnosis and treatment must be done by a qualified doctor or medical officer.

sections.label: Heart Attack Warning Signs: Call 112 or Go to Hospital Immediately
items: Pain, pressure, or constriction in the centre of the chest lasting more than 30 minutes
Pain spreading to the jaw, neck, arms, shoulders, or back
Shortness of breath along with chest discomfort
Nausea with chest pain
Loss of consciousness

sections.label: Stroke Warning Signs: Call 112 or Go to Hospital Immediately
items: Sudden weakness, paralysis, or numbness on one side of the face, arm, or leg
Loss of speech or sudden difficulty speaking or understanding speech
Dimness or loss of vision, particularly in one eye
Unexplained dizziness, unsteadiness, or sudden falls
Sudden severe headache or loss of consciousness
Any of these signs in a person with high blood pressure must be treated as a medical emergency, refer immediately to a Community Health Centre or hospital

sections.label: Lifestyle Measures for Persons with High Blood Pressure
items: Stop all use of tobacco, smoking or chewing tobacco significantly raises blood pressure and risk of heart attack
Reduce alcohol intake
Reduce salt intake, limit to a maximum of 1 teaspoon (5 grams) of salt per day for the whole family
Reduce consumption of oily, fried, and fatty foods
Reduce intake of refined cereals (maida), sugar, and sweet beverages
Eat more fresh fruits, vegetables, whole grains, and whole pulses
Maintain a healthy weight, losing weight if overweight significantly reduces blood pressure
Be physically active, at least 30 minutes of brisk walking or moderate activity daily
Manage stress, practice relaxation techniques, take breaks, maintain social connections
Take blood pressure medicines every day as prescribed, do not stop on your own even if you feel fine
Get blood pressure checked at least once a month if on treatment
Attend regular follow-up at the Primary Health Centre or sub-centre as advised

sections.label: See a Doctor
items: Hypertension is called the silent killer because it usually has no symptoms, the only way to detect it is to measure blood pressure
All adults aged 30 years and above should have their blood pressure checked at least once a year even if they feel well

A blood pressure reading of 140 mm Hg systolic (upper number) or 90 mm Hg diastolic (lower number) or above on a single reading should prompt referral to a medical officer for confirmation and further management
Frequent headaches, especially at the back of the head in the morning, can sometimes be a symptom of very high blood pressure
Any person with high blood pressure who develops a new symptom or illness, they are at higher risk of complications
Family history of heart attack or stroke, screening and prevention are very important

sections.label: Go to Hospital Without Delay
items: Any heart attack or stroke warning sign listed above, these are medical emergencies
Very severe headache with high blood pressure and visual disturbance or confusion, may indicate hypertensive emergency
A known hypertensive patient who has stopped their medication and is now feeling unwell
A hypertensive patient with chest pain, breathlessness, or swelling of the legs, may indicate heart failure

prevention_note.label: Preventing Heart Attack and Stroke in Hypertensive Patients
items: All adults above 30 years should be screened annually for both high blood pressure and diabetes
Blood pressure and blood sugar must be monitored regularly in high-risk individuals, those with a family history of heart attack or stroke
Anyone who experiences heart attack or stroke warning signs must seek immediate medical care, every minute matters
